transcript.text: my washin mashine wont turn on at all no lights nothin

With absolutely no lights or response, this is a power-supply fault rather than a door or programme problem. The most common causes are the wall socket or an isolator/switch, a loose or damaged plug/lead, then an internal incoming-power part such as the mains filter; the control board is further down the list. 1. Unplug the washing machine. Check whether another small appliance works from the same socket. If there is a separate wall switch or fused spur, make sure it is switched on. A dead socket/spur points to the house supply rather than the washer. 2. Check the washer plug is fully seated and inspect the lead from plug to machine for cuts, crushing, scorching or looseness. Do not use it if the lead or plug is damaged. 3. If there was a pop, bang, burning smell, or a fuse/trip operated when it died, leave it unplugged. Do not keep replacing fuses or repeatedly try to power it up; it needs an electrician or appliance engineer to trace the cause. If the socket most likely works, the plug/lead look sound, and the machine remains completely dead, an engineer should check the internal mains filter, incoming wiring and power-supply section safely.

its built in behind a cupboard door so i cant reach the plug or pull it out. other stuff in the kitchen works tho, my kettle is fine. no burning smell or anything. is there a switch i should look for?

Yes. For an integrated washing machine, look in the cupboard beside it, the sink-base cupboard, or sometimes high on the wall/inside an adjacent cabinet for a small white switched unit. It may have a rocker switch marked ON/OFF, sometimes a red neon light, and often a removable fuse carrier; this is the washing machine’s fused spur/isolator. 1. With dry hands, look for that switch and make sure it is set to ON. Do not remove the fuse carrier or open anything.
2. Also check whether there is a kitchen appliance isolation switch above the worktop, sometimes labelled for appliances. Turn it on if it is off. Your kettle working shows the kitchen has power, but it does not prove the washing machine’s own switched spur is live. If you find the switch already on and the washer remains completely dead, the likely causes move to its hidden plug/lead connection or an internal incoming-power fault such as the mains filter or power-supply section. As it cannot be safely pulled out or isolated by you, an appliance engineer would be the sensible next step rather than dismantling the cupboard or machine.
ok i looked and theres a row of switches above the worktop and one says washer and its OFF. my flatmate must of switched it off when she was cleaning. should i turn it back on?

Yes — switch the one labelled “washer” back to ON, using dry hands. That is very likely why it has been completely dead. Then check whether the washer lights/display come back on. If it does, the fault is resolved; you can select a programme as normal. If the switch immediately trips back off, or there is any smell, crackling or heat from the switch, turn it off again and arrange an electrician or appliance engineer. If the switch stays on but the machine is still completely dead, the isolator may not be supplying it or there may be an internal incoming-power fault, so it will need an engineer because the appliance cannot be safely isolated or pulled out.
ok i turned it back on and the machine lights up now and works! thanks

[Heading: Likely cause: power switch]
That has resolved it — the washer’s isolation switch being off was the cause, not a fault with the machine. It may help to label it clearly or let your flatmate know that switch feeds the washer. Is there anything else you need help with?
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
